source.description: Classify one structured event using the following public policy. Critical means risk is TRUE or action is change; critical cases require review. Unknown external: risk UNKNOWN in context internal returns uncertain. Unknown risk otherwise prefers deny at priority 90. Trusted means role is operator outside context internal; a trusted approve prefers allow at priority 80. Action export in context internal prefers review at priority 70. Role admin or context partner prefers deny at priority 40. Trusted cases forbid deny. All other declared roles prefer allow at priority 1. Required labels override preferences. Abstention or conflicting required labels returns uncertain. Forbidden labels are removed; the remaining highest-priority preference wins.
requirements: Critical means risk is TRUE or action is change; critical cases require review.

repairs.original_source:
predicate Critical(event):
    (event.risk == TRUE) or (event.action == change)

predicate Trusted(event):
    (event.role == operator) and (event.context != internal)

predicate UnknownExternal(event):
    (event.risk == UNKNOWN) and (event.context == internal)

rule CriticalCase:
    when Critical(event)
    then require label = review

rule UnknownExternalCase:
    when UnknownExternal(event)
    then abstain

rule UnknownRisk:
    when (event.risk == UNKNOWN) and (not (UnknownExternal(event)))
    then prefer label = deny priority 90

rule TrustedApprove:
    when (Trusted(event)) and (event.action == approve)
    then prefer label = allow priority 80, forbid label = deny

rule ExportInternal:
    when (event.action == export) and (event.context == internal)
    then prefer label = review priority 70

rule AdminOrPartner:
    when (event.role == admin) or (event.context == partner)
    then prefer label = deny priority 40

rule OtherRoles:
    when ((event.role != operator) and (event.role != admin)) and (event.role != guest)
    then prefer label = allow priority 1

deployment_description: Classify one structured event using the supplied compiled instructions. The allowed outputs are allow, review, deny, uncertain. These names are arbitrary symbols, so do not infer their meaning. Copy the output stated by the matching compiled instruction.
